messages:
IncidentBot: Pager triggered for inference-prod-eu (route: embeddings) — severity: page :rotating_light:. Runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/kvcache-eviction — please acknowledge.
Alex T: I'm primary on this shift, ack. Taking the pager now. Starting triage — @Sam P are you on secondary?
Sam P: Yep I'm secondary, standing by. Ping me if you want me to take the bridge or run the routing rollback.
Maria G: Heads up — customer-impact: ~10% of embedding requests returning 5xx in eu-west-1 since 09:12 UTC. CS notified to stand by. Ticket #INC-1715.
Alex T: Any recent runtime/model deploys in the last 30m?
Jamal R: No deploys. Quick glance at infra: redis-proxy shows repeated eviction spikes -> probably prefix cache thrash. Shared runbook above has the triage steps.
Alex T: Can you run the quick mitigation (scale redis-proxy + bump TTL) and paste commands here?
Jamal R: On it. Commands I'm running:
```
kubectl -n infra scale deploy/redis-proxy --replicas=4
redis-cli -h redis-proxy setex prefix_ttl 300
```
I'll tail logs and report.
IncidentBot: Attached log snapshot: /ops/logs/1715001234-snapshot.log
Jamal R: Log tail sample:
```
[2024-07-05T09:14:12Z] eviction: prefix=kv_prefix_123 size=1.2GB thrash=true
[2024-07-05T09:14:13Z] eviction: prefix=kv_prefix_123 size=1.3GB thrash=true
```
Looks like repeated re-population causing a loop.
Sam P: If scaling/TLL bump doesn't stabilize, fallback option: route embeddings -> model-b (lower capacity but stable). Routing console quick command:
```
route set embeddings model-b --weight 100
```
Maria G: Quick comms note for CS: "We are mitigating a cache eviction issue affecting embeddings in EU. Mitigation in progress; we'll update within 15m." Please post to #customer-impact.
Alex T: Added incident doc: https://redwood.internal/incidents/1715001234 — updating timeline and mitigation steps now.
Jamal R: Scale and TTL update completed. Metrics: p99 latency for embeddings dropped from ~1.1s -> ~320ms within ~60s. Error rate down from 10% -> 1.2%.
Sam P: Nice. Plan: keep replicas=4 for 30m, monitor. If errors spike again, execute routing rollback to model-b and escalate to oncall-ml.
Alex T: For next handoff: primary remains me until 09:45 UTC unless things regress. If you take over, copy incident doc and include these quick actions in the handoff note.
Maria G: Runbook quick pointers (copying paste for visibility):
1) Check redis-proxy pod health: `kubectl get pods -n infra -l app=redis-proxy`
2) Increase replicas: `kubectl scale deploy/redis-proxy --replicas=N`
3) Increase prefix TTL: `redis-cli -h redis-proxy setex prefix_ttl 300`
4) If still thrashing, route embeddings -> model-b: `route set embeddings model-b --weight 100`
5) Notify #customer-impact and update incident doc.
Also add to postmortem: consider persistent warming and stronger prefix-level guards.
IncidentBot: Incident status changed: mitigated — monitoring.
Alex T: Thanks team. Leaving a short handoff note: primary till 09:45 UTC, metrics look stable, replicas kept at 4, TTL=300. I'll write a blameless postmortem tomorrow and propose a remediation ticket for prefix warming.
Sam P: Acknowledged. Ready to take over if latency creeps back up. :thumbsup:
Jamal R: Dropping a small snippet for runbook inclusion:
```
# quick-check
kubectl -n infra logs deploy/redis-proxy --tail=200
redis-cli info memory
```
Keep an eye on eviction metrics and prefix churn.
Maria G: Publishing a short customer blip now. I'll update the incident doc when CS confirms message posted.
Alex T: Good work. Closing thread once we see 15m stable window."
